title: Trait swap in the two-kind Marangoni rods: whichever surfactant kind carries the Marangoni drive gains share over the neutral twin, on 6/6 paired comparisons (3 seeds x 2 assignments), with no kind conversions; the swimmers out-divide the non-swimmers
summary: Control for 20261026T0630-c34-marangoni-two-kinds: the same world and seeds with the trait swapped (kind A mar=0, kind B marB=40). The swimming kind B ends at 0.82, 0.77 and 0.94 of the pure rods at frame 185 on seeds 0-2, against 0.69, 0.27 and 0.79 for B in the neutral twin (both kinds swim), so together with the original assignment the swimming kind beats its neutral share on 6 of 6 paired comparisons (gains +0.13 to +0.50). No rod switches kind along any labkit track in the 9 runs, so the gain comes from division: swimmer parents make 19/18/28 persistent splits here against 2/6/0 for non-swimmers (25/19/11 vs 2/10/15 in the original arm). Limits: 3 seeds, one T=1000 window, the 6 comparisons share their neutral runs, and the mechanism (why swimmers divide more: more fuel met, or Marangoni-driven elongation that triggers fission) is not measured.

finding.operator: heritable surfactant kinds with majority-feedback copying; Marangoni drive on one kind
finding.control: neutral twin (both kinds swim) on the same seeds, and the trait swapped between kinds
finding.result: swimmer share above neutral on 6/6 paired comparisons (+0.13 to +0.50 at frame 185); 0 kind switches in 9 runs; swimmer vs non-swimmer persistent splits 19/2, 18/6, 28/0 (swap) and 19/10, 25/2, 11/15 (original)
